1 Auctor huius collectionis fuit sine dubio ipse Eleutherius Eleus, qui non merus
librarius erat, etsi Mitylenis a. 1388 priorem partem huius codicis, a. 1390 codicem
Taurinensem 4 descripserit, sed astrologus quoque, utpote Iohannes Abramius, qui
codicem Florentinum 10 a. 1382 confecit (Catal. Flor., p. 38, n. 1), eum magistrum
suum praedicaverit (cf. supra cap. ριγ'). Ad hunc Eleutherium referenda sunt
sections.en: 1 The author of this collection was without doubt Eleutherius of Elis himself, who was not a mere librarian, although he copied the first part of this codex in Mytilene in 1388, and the Turin codex 4 in 1390, but also an astrologer, inasmuch as John Abramius, who completed the Florentine codex 10 in 1382 (Catal. Flor., p. 38, n. 1), proclaimed him his master (cf. above ch. 113). To this Eleutherius are to be referred

summary.headline: Chapters on Martial and Mundane Astrology
summary.text: Continuation of the Angelican codex catalogue, listing chapters 137–148 on harmful degrees, lunar applications, conjunctions, tyranny, lost things, besieged or ruined cities, martial elections, war, eclipse nodes, and right and left configurations. It records the Mytilene subscription of 1388 by Eleutherios of Elis and identifies a 312-chapter collection of Apotelesmatics.
